idiom_name: MAUI Behavior<T> with OnAttachedTo/OnDetachingFrom; BindableProperty + observable state holder
implementation_notes: The closest framework mechanism is the .NET MAUI behaviour: deriving from Behavior or Behavior<T> and overriding OnAttachedTo/OnDetachingFrom adds reusable functionality to controls without subclassing them, and the framework calls that pair as the control's lifecycle, which is where events are registered and, crucially, unregistered. State comes from BindableProperty plus INotifyPropertyChanged (or an observable model such as a CommunityToolkit.Mvvm view-model), and a reusable state-holder class shared through dependency injection replaces the hook unit; Blazor composes reusable logic through components with parameters and cascading values rather than by function calls. The docs warn that static attached behaviours are hard to give state, so per-control state belongs to Behavior<T> instances. Unlike hooks there is no call-order slot model, so lifetime stays explicit: whatever OnAttachedTo subscribes, OnDetachingFrom must release. The classic form is still justified when the behaviour really is the screen's own state rather than a reusable unit: keep a plain view-model plus declarative bindings instead of attaching yet another behaviour to a control.
pitfalls: MAUI does not set the BindingContext of a behaviour, so binding-dependent state must be passed explicitly rather than relying on inherited bindings.
Every event subscribed in OnAttachedTo must be detached in OnDetachingFrom; a behaviour shared through a style is applied to many controls and leaks per-control handlers otherwise.
State in a static attached behaviour is shared by design and the docs call it difficult to give state - keep per-control state in Behavior<T> instances or an injected state holder.
